scope: Curated code-to-task trace for robots.txt reuse across HPLT and OpenEuroLLM. Literal evidence only; not a runtime correctness or legal compliance audit.

sources.phrase: adopt and adapt the intermediate step by jaume
sources.meaning: The existing pipeline is explicitly named as work to adapt; this is not newly discovered unrelated duplication.
Separate opt-out policy issue requiring decisions about applicability and retroactive filtering.
HPLT Stage 1 stores robots.txt captures separately for later processing.
Existing HPLT batch produces an indexed set of disallowed URLs from captured robots.txt.
The existing parser is scoped to these user agents and requires review against OpenEuroLLM use cases.
HPLT already has a compiled Rust matcher for robots allow/disallow patterns against an URL index.
Prior HPLT script invokes the tool generating line-aligned allowance annotations.
Stage 3 optionally reads allowed.zst; if absent it does not apply this sitewide filter.

sources.phrase: If present, this file will be used
sources.meaning: HPLT documents that allowance filtering depends on presence of allowed.zst.
Existing OpenEuroLLM code checks X-Robots-Tag and HTML robots directives, not the cross-page historical sitewide robots index.
OpenEuroLLM extracts robots.txt response records for a separate downstream processing step.
The current page-local filtering rules are documented separately from sitewide robots.txt evaluation.

review_checks: Confirm the intended crawler user-agent policy and robots.txt group precedence, wildcard handling and allow/disallow specificity with tests.
Decide the temporal policy for robots.txt captures and missing/ambiguous captures; avoid assuming one historical capture applies retroactively.
For IA or other crawls requiring post-hoc robots filtering, explicitly require allowed.zst or fail the job rather than silently continuing.
Check URL normalization (scheme, www, ports, percent encoding) and sample allow/disallow precedence before reusing a URL index.
Verify line count, line order, and key consistency among metadata.zst, allowed.zst and downstream Stage 3 outputs.
Keep HTTP/meta/TDM reservations separate from sitewide robots.txt decisions; document combined exclusion policy.
Confirm existing stakeholders have already scheduled this adaptation before posting any duplicate implementation request.
